method: Qualitative pretest score from current paid alternatives, willingness-to-pay signals, purchase intent clarity, AI fulfillability, distribution fit, saturation, and regulatory risk. This is a screening score, not market size or conversion data.

shortlist.why: Extremely high-intent search moment; incumbent takes 35% of recovered compensation; clear money-saving wedge. Risk: passenger-rights/legal copy must stay self-service and accurate.
High-stakes one-off moment with large economic upside; live AI alternatives charge from about EUR7.99 while human negotiation services charge hundreds to thousands. Strong value-to-price ratio.
Deadline-driven emotional purchase; direct competitors publish one-time prices around $29-$49. Fulfillment is fully digital and immediate.
Direct consumer pain and proven one-time pricing around $9-$50. Strong social distribution, but crowded; offer must include diagnosis/photo ordering rather than generic bio writing.
High-intent deadline-driven need; many paid interview prep tools charge roughly $9-$25+ monthly or per pack. Crowded, but job-specific answer scaffolding can be delivered instantly.

hold.reason: Large demand but severe commoditization and generous free tiers from many incumbents.
Good intent, but low ticket and numerous cheap/free letter generators; may work later as success-fee recovery rather than $7 template.
Clear pain but low willingness to pay for generic complaint writing.
High pain in competitive rental markets, but weak evidence of standalone paid demand.
Huge market, heavily saturated by free and $10-$15/mo AI study apps.
Paid party-planning apps exist, but strongest paid wedge appears visual decor generation rather than text planning.
Willingness to pay exists, but full wardrobe apps already offer far richer persistent products.
Very crowded; paid itinerary prices can be as low as $1-$5 per trip and many free alternatives exist.
Real family packing pain but incumbent family travel apps bundle this with much richer functionality.
Massive category but generic 30-day plans are easily substituted by established AI language apps and general LLMs.
Useful problem but free/low-cost moving planners make a one-off $7 text plan weak.
Strong pain but cancellation managers commonly offer free tracking and direct cancellation guidance.
Listing copy already has many free tools and agent-focused products; private-seller frequency is low.
Listing platforms themselves increasingly generate descriptions with AI, weakening the standalone wedge.
Abundant free printable templates; weak reason to pay for the current offer.
